text.p: British banking group Barclays Plc said on Wednesday it planned to buy back up to 26 million ordinary shares representing around 1.7 percent of its issued ordinary share capital.

Barclays later said it had bought 9.2 million shares under the programme at 1137.27 pence per share. The news came just a week after the bank disappointed the stock market by not announcing a buy back with its 1996 results.
Barclays shares rose strongly on news of the buy back, touching a high of 1165 pence before settling for a gain of five at 1127.

"While it is encouraging in many ways that there are not enough sellers of the shares at the current price to enable us to complete our planned purchase this morning, we remain committed to returning capital to shareholders and shall be looking to buy further shares as appropriate," said chief executive Martin Taylor.
Barclays said it was repurchasing its shares from brokers BZW Securities Limited and Cazenove & Co.
The buyback is Barclay's fourth repurchase of shares, but differs from the previous ones in that BZW and brokers Cazenove are buying the shares as principals rather than as agents for the company.

Accordingly, normal UK tax rules for selling shares in the market will generally apply, rather than special rules which apply to direct repurchase of shares by a company. Barclays said shareholders should obtain their own tax advice on consequences of participating in the buyback.
At present market prices, the total share buyback would be worth just under 300 million pounds ($490.6 million).
In 1995, Barclays returned 180 million pounds ($294.5 million) of capital to shareholders. In February 1996, 306 million pounds were returned and 470 million in August 1996.
It said it was aiming to maximise shareholder value and noted that repurchases boosted earnings per share. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
